newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Greenpeace urges Cyprus declaration on park.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace urges Cyprus declaration on park.

text.p: Greenpeace on Thursday urged the Cypriot government to declare an uninhabited peninsula in the north west a protected area, and to ban development which has marred other coastlines of the eastern Mediterranean island.

Successive Cypriot governments have pledged to turn the Akamas peninsula into a national park, but have failed to make good on the promises. Local environmentalists are concerned the delay could pave the way for development of the area, while locals strongly oppose recommendations that development be banned on land belonging to them.

"The government of Cyprus must stop hiding behind the excuse that the villagers are being mistreated by the declaration of this national park," said Mario Damato of the Greenpeace Mediterranean Office.
"It is two or three big influential landowners who own the crucial land that has to be dealt with, not the villagers," he told a news conference.

A group of Greenpeace activists who arrived on the island last Saturday aboard the "Arctic Sunrise" staged a protest earlier on Thursday at the site of a hotel under construction in the Akamas by the family firm of Cypriot Foreign Minister Alecos Michaelides.

Greenpeace and local pressure groups say his family company has ignored World Bank recommendations for restrained development in the area which they say is an important nesting site for endangered green and loggerhead turtles.
Instead, they say, the Cypriot government relaxed normal building restrictions in the area earlier this year, giving his company the green light for the construction of a 350-bed hotel there.
"It is an abuse of the area and an abuse of power," said local campaigner Yiannos Ioannou.
Michaelides' family firm has denied the allegations.
